title: Controller initialization
equipment: Variable-speed booster pump with recirculation valve
physicalPurpose: Start automatic discharge-pressure control from the actual running pressure and valve position instead of arbitrary controller and filter histories.
objective: Initialize controller and filter histories from the running booster pump, distinguish Disabled, Manual, Auto, and Track authority, and block Auto until startup state is qualified.

simplifications: The first-order pressure model represents one bounded operating region and does not model pump curves, check valves, cavitation, or network demand transients.
Actual valve-position feedback is supplied independently of the controller output so startup state cannot be inferred from a stale command.
The zero-state and settle-interlock-bypass case is simulation-only diagnostic evidence and shall not be used on a physical pump.

baseline.limitation: Arbitrary zero controller and filter histories produce a first request of 10 percent and filtered pressure of 0.198 bar on a pump already operating at 40 percent and 6 bar.

change.decision: Copy current pressure, setpoint, and actual valve position into filter and controller histories atomically, retain Manual authority until the filter is qualified, then permit Auto.

disturbances: Repeat at 20, 40, and 70 percent equilibrium valve positions

acceptance.window: first permitted automatic update at each 20, 40, and 70 percent equilibrium
first automatic update with deliberate settle-interlock bypass

abortPredicates: Pressure, valve feedback, or controller value is nonfinite
Pressure or requested/applied valve command leaves its hard limit
Automatic authority is requested without complete initialization or settled-filter qualification
safety.restorationMode: Station Disabled with the declared 30 percent safe recirculation command
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Do not bypass the filter-settle interlock or exercise startup transitions on a physical pump without reviewed topology, independent valve feedback, protection, and explicit approval.

video.viewerOutcome: Initialize a running loop from actual process and actuator state and explain why Auto remains blocked until state is qualified.
requiredVisibleEvidence: actual, requested, and applied valve values

learning.context: A booster pump is already operating when the controller starts. Pressure and valve position therefore have physical values before any PID update is allowed.
learning.reason: Lesson 26 showed that output and previous signals are controller state. Arbitrary startup state can command a valve movement unrelated to the running station.
theory: Raw pressure is the sensor value; filtered pressure is the value used by the controller. Actual valve feedback, requested command, and applied command are separate signals and may differ.

Initialization copies present SP, PV, nominal output, applied output, and filter input into retained histories. It performs no feedback, integration, differentiation, limiting, or actuator command calculation.
Control.PID supports Manual, Auto, and Track. Disabled is station supervision outside PIDMode: it does not call the controller and applies the declared safe command.
Auto remains blocked under Manual authority until initialization is complete and filtered pressure stays within 0.01 bar of raw pressure for three consecutive updates.
learning.workedPrediction: The plant equilibrium is pressure = 2 bar + 0.1 bar/% times valve position. Valve positions 20, 40, and 70 percent therefore correspond to 4, 6, and 9 bar. With SP equal to PV and controller output initialized from actual valve feedback, the first Auto request equals the existing valve position.
practicalPreparation: Verify raw and filtered pressure, independent actual valve feedback, requested and applied commands, requested and active authority, controller-ready, filter-settled, startup-blocked, limits, and simulation label.
Start Disabled at the 30 percent safe command; use the 100 ms task and never bypass the settle interlock outside the declared simulation baseline.
learning.baseline: At 6 bar and 40 percent valve position, initialize filter and controller histories to zero and bypass the settle interlock in simulation. Record the first 10 percent command and 0.198 bar filtered value.
learning.change: Restore, initialize from current pressure, setpoint, and actual valve feedback, wait for three settled-filter updates under Manual authority, then permit Auto. Repeat at the 20, 40, and 70 percent equilibria.
learning.comparison: Compare first-update valve mismatch, immediate filter initialization error, readiness, settle indication, startup blocking, active authority, and any requested-to-applied difference under identical initial conditions.
learning.validation: Require measured-state valve mismatch and filter error to be at most 1e-9, expose at least 10 percentage points of zero-state mismatch, and hold the 40 percent simulated equilibrium within 0.05 bar and 0.5 percentage points over 10 seconds.
learning.explanation: A correct PID equation cannot infer the already-running actuator position or repair invented filter history. Those values must enter initialization explicitly before feedback receives authority.
learning.transfer: Use the same startup discipline for any running process. Lesson 28 tests whether state remains aligned when authority changes after startup and establishes bumpless transfer.
